entities.summary: Elsbeth Stagel was a Dominican nun and prioress of the Töss Convent, a prominent female leader in medieval Switzerland during the 14th century. Born around 1320, Stagel played a crucial role in the reform of the convent, implementing new organizational and economic systems that improved the lives of the nuns and increased the convent's influence in the region. The Töss Convent became a model for other Dominican convents, reflecting Stagel's commitment to the spiritual and social welfare of the women under her care. Her legacy as a pioneering female leader in the Catholic Church has endured, inspiring generations of women in religious orders. Stagel's remarkable life and work serve as a testament to the power of women's leadership and the importance of promoting social and economic reform in the face of patriarchal norms.
